title: US destroys five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and off Kharg
note: US Central Command said the Revolutionary Guard tried twice in two days to hit a US warship with ballistic missiles, and that in reply US forces ordered the crews off and struck four Iranian crude carriers in the Gulf of Oman and one near Kharg Island, rendering them inoperable. The command later put the week's total at ten Iranian tankers destroyed, calling them part of a shadow network that funds the Guard.
place: Gulf of Oman and Kharg Island
metricName: Iranian oil tankers struck in one night (10 in the week, per CENTCOM)
limitations: Ship counts are the US command's own statements; Iran confirmed five tankers were hit but has not confirmed the weekly total.

title: Iran says it hit two US vessels and eight tankers near Hormuz; US denies any warship struck
note: The Revolutionary Guard said its naval forces attacked two American vessels and eight tankers that tried to cross a stretch of the Strait of Hormuz it had declared forbidden, warned of imminent attacks on tankers near Bahrain and Kuwait, told crews to evacuate, and extended a restricted zone from Chabahar. US Central Command replied that no US Navy warship had been struck and that every attempted attack failed. Brent crude crossed 100 dollars a barrel the same morning. The largest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began in February.
metricName: vessels Iran says it attacked (2 US vessels, 8 tankers)
limitations: The two sides' accounts contradict each other; damage to the tankers and any casualties were not independently confirmed when checked.

title: Iran fires missiles at the US-used Al-Azraq base in Jordan
note: Iran's foreign ministry said its armed forces struck US bases and facilities in Jordan, which it accused of supporting US attacks on Iran, as a response to the tanker strikes. The Revolutionary Guard claimed hangars used by US fighter jets at Al-Azraq were destroyed. The base attack widens the exchange from the Gulf to a third country's territory.
limitations: Damage claims are Iranian; the US had not commented on the base attack when this report was published, and interception figures circulating elsewhere could not be checked against a primary source.

title: Yemen's government forces open a counteroffensive aimed at Sanaa
note: Forces loyal to Yemen's internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia, reported rocket and drone strikes and ground battles in Taiz, al-Bayda and al-Jawf, the main gateway to the capital, and said the campaign's aim is to retake Sanaa. The Houthis said they repelled the al-Jawf push and that an air strike on a prison in al-Hazm killed at least seven people. Yemen's civil war, dormant for years, is back as a front of the Gulf war.
metricName: reported killed in the al-Hazm prison strike, per the Houthis
limitations: Battlefield claims come from the two sides; the prison casualty figure is Houthi-reported.

title: Pakistan carries a Saudi warning to Iran to rein in the Houthis as Riyadh strikes Yemen
note: After Houthi missiles and drones hit an air base at Khamis Mushait and oil sites in nearby cities, wounding 73, Pakistan delivered a Saudi warning to Tehran to restrain the group. A Houthi spokesman said Saudi warplanes flew 54 strikes across Yemeni provinces in twelve hours. Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish military officials meeting in Riyadh agreed that none of their troops would enter Yemen and that any retaliation would be launched from Saudi soil. Two Iranian sources told the agency Tehran had asked the Houthis to attack the kingdom and promised money and weapons.
metricName: Saudi strikes across Yemen in twelve hours, per the Houthis
limitations: The Pakistani channel and the Iranian instruction to the Houthis rest on anonymous sources in a wire exclusive; the strike count is a Houthi figure.

title: RSF drone strike on a North Kordofan courthouse kills at least 13
note: A Rapid Support Forces drone hit the judicial headquarters in Um Rawaba, North Kordofan, during working hours when the area outside the court was crowded, killing at least 13 people and wounding more than 20 according to local sources. The paramilitary has stepped up drone attacks on army-held towns as the war passes its third year.
limitations: Casualty figures come from local medical and civil sources, not an independent count.

title: US and Poland sign a 4 billion dollar military financing loan guarantee
note: In Warsaw the two governments signed a 4 billion dollar Foreign Military Financing loan guarantee, which the State Department says brings total US support for Poland's rearmament to nearly 20 billion dollars, on top of F-35s delivered in May, Patriot batteries, HIMARS and Apache helicopters. A mobilization indicator on NATO's eastern flank rather than a combat event.
metricName: loan guarantee signed (nearly 20 billion USD cumulative)
limitations: Figures are the signing government's; the loan guarantee is financing, not a delivery of equipment.

title: Norway says a Russian drone came close to the plane carrying Ukraine's president out of Moldova
note: Norway's prime minister said a Russian jet-powered drone came near the aircraft carrying Ukraine's president as it left Chisinau on Tuesday for a state funeral in Oslo; Moldovan authorities had detected an unidentified drone in their airspace and grounded several flights. The Ukrainian president's office disputed the characterisation as overstated. Whether a near miss or an airspace violation, the incident put a head of state's aircraft inside the war's drone envelope over a non-belligerent country.
limitations: The Norwegian account did not give its source or the distance involved, and Kyiv played the incident down.

title: North Korea's leader thanks soldiers on 'overseas military operations' at the founding anniversary
note: At the 78th founding anniversary in Pyongyang the leader extended what state media called special gratitude to commanders and soldiers taking part in overseas military operations, an open reference to the estimated 14,000 to 15,000 troops sent to fight for Russia since late 2024. South Korea's intelligence service put North Korean killed and wounded at around 6,000 by February, and its defence ministry said in late August that preparations for a further deployment continue.
metricName: North Korean troops deployed to Russia since late 2024 (Western and South Korean estimates)
limitations: Troop and casualty numbers are foreign intelligence estimates; Pyongyang's statement did not name the theatre.

title: Canada agrees a 350 million dollar air-defence interceptor package for Ukraine
note: After meeting Ukraine's president in Calgary, Canada's prime minister announced a C$350 million package to buy air-defence interceptors through the US programme that lets third countries purchase Patriot-class missiles for Kyiv, which is running low on interceptors as Russia steps up ballistic and jet-drone attacks on logistics and economic targets. He also set a goal of producing millions of drones within two years, a third for Ukraine, and repeated support for Ukraine's NATO and EU bids.
limitations: Which interceptors and when they arrive were not disclosed.

title: Britain, Norway and the US disclose that they confronted a Russian subsea-cable sabotage exercise near Svalbard
note: The three allies say that in the spring they tracked and confronted Russian vessels from the navy's undersea-warfare directorate as deep-sea submersibles rehearsed deploying equipment able to cut critical cables in Arctic waters near Svalbard, and stopped the exercise from finishing. British and Norwegian officials then took the findings to Moscow as a deterrent. Western services believe the Kremlin is expanding sabotage across Europe to probe the alliance's mutual-defence commitment.
limitations: The operation happened months earlier and is dated here by disclosure; details come from unnamed Western officials and Russia has not responded.

title: Security Council holds its Iran non-proliferation briefing, then a Yemen meeting the same day
note: The Council's 10218th meeting took up Iran under the Non-Proliferation item, the scheduled 90-day briefing on the sanctions committee revived when the European three triggered snapback a year ago, with the expert panel's mandate due to expire on 27 September; the 10219th meeting that afternoon was on Yemen. The Council remains split on the Iran file, and the sessions came the day after the atomic agency reported more than a year without access to key Iranian sites.
limitations: The meeting summary was not yet posted when checked; the agenda item comes from the Council's September programme of work.

title: US strike on a suspected drug boat in the Caribbean kills three, the 69th such strike
note: Southern Command said a joint task force carried out a lethal strike on a go-fast vessel on a trafficking route in the Caribbean, killing three people it called narco-terrorists, without releasing evidence. It was the 69th publicly acknowledged strike in the year-long campaign, which has killed at least 230 people and which rights groups and UN experts describe as unlawful.
limitations: The identity of the vessel and its cargo rest on the military's statement alone.

title: August 2026 was the joint hottest month ever recorded, 1.65 C above pre-industrial
note: The Copernicus Climate Change Service put the global average surface air temperature for August at 16.96 C, the warmest August in its record and level with July 2023 as the hottest month of any name, 1.65 C above the pre-industrial baseline and the first month above 1.5 C since November 2025. Sea surface temperature outside the polar oceans set a record as strong El Nino conditions build in the Pacific; western Europe had its hottest summer, passing 2003.
metricName: global mean surface air temperature, August 2026
limitations: A single-month reanalysis figure; the twelve-month mean is the measure the Paris threshold refers to.

title: Declassified papers show Spain was warned a day before 72,000 people crossed into Ceuta
note: Documents released by the Spanish government show its intelligence service told Moroccan and Ceuta authorities on 29 July that social media groups reaching about 180,000 people were calling for a mass crossing the next day. At least 72,000 people crossed from Morocco on 30 and 31 July, most by swimming round the fence; at least 100 died. Most were returned but up to 5,000 remain in camps and on the streets, with local unrest, blocked aid and accusations that Morocco eased the surge.
metricName: crossed into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July
limitations: Crossing and death figures are from the city's mayor; the role of Moroccan authorities is alleged, not established.
